expectations.text: B1: Diagnoses and gives a minimal fix or hint
expectations.evidence: Diagnosis: 'Under churn the heap fills with holes smaller than any incoming request, so malloc calls sbrk again even though total free space is enough'. Minimal fix given as a short snippet in free(): 'after marking the block free, look at the next physical block and absorb it' with ~5 lines of code (next-merge only, 'do the next-merge first'). Coaches with a 2-minute differential test rather than writing the implementation (FILES WRITTEN: 0).

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Ends with concrete command 'cc -o churn churn.c mymalloc.c && ./churn' and expected output 'A: sbrk calls = 1, heap top constant / B: c == a, sbrk calls = 1', plus 'rerun your original workload — the sbrk counter should plateau'.

expectations.text: B3: Identifies missing block reuse/splitting/coalescing of adjacent free blocks
expectations.evidence: 'A flat, B calls sbrk → coalescing is missing. This is the likely one.' Also covers reuse ('malloc's fit test must accept size <= hole->size') and splitting ('if malloc() splits blocks, the remainder must be written back as a well-formed free block in the list').

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: SHELL COMMANDS RUN: only 'ls -a'; other calls are glob and read of a skill file. No install commands, no files written (FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT: 0); the cc/churn command is a suggestion to the learner and writes inside the project dir.
